title: VibeMaxxing decision-to-implementation traceability
description: One row for every decision in conformance/planning/decisions-v1.json, owned by the P-1140F track. P-1140E froze structural traceability at D-001..D-069 and a later decision must not silently expand a closed program's evidence set, so this is the second matrix PF-063 called for rather than a widening of range(1, 70). The rule it makes checkable comes from docs/planning/decision-traceability/README.md: a decision is covered only when it has a normative owner, an implementation work unit, machine or state ownership, platform behaviour, and executable acceptance evidence.

implementation_bearing.description: Whether the decision constrains the product. A decision about the planning program itself — validator behaviour, document structure, gate process — does not, and saying so is the honest row rather than a manufactured owner.

reason.description: Why the decision is not implementation-bearing. Required when implementation_bearing is false; an unexplained exclusion cannot be told apart from an omission.

implementation_owner.description: A work-unit series or a real path. The literal `unassigned` is permitted only alongside owner_gap_reason: a decision that constrains the product but that no unit owns is a real coverage gap, and writing a plausible owner to fill the cell would hide it.

owner_gap_reason.description: Required when implementation_owner is `unassigned`. What is missing, so the gap is counted rather than papered over.

allOf.comment: `unassigned` is a claim that no unit owns the decision, and a claim needs its reason. Describing this in a property description without expressing it here is how a rule becomes decorative.

cell.description: A literal pipe would shift every column to its right when this row is rendered into the traceability tables.
